newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond prices fall in becalmed, wary market.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond prices fall in becalmed, wary market.

text.p: Danish bond prices slipped undramatically in a becalmed market, cautiously treading water ahead of U.S. key data and the British general election later in the week, with dealers predicting continued uncertainty and low investor activity.

"Investors are on the sideline, the market is ultra-calm. Uncertainty about overseas developments means that turnover will stay low at least until Tuesday's U.S. NAPM, GDP and other data," one dealer said.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.18 point from the opening at 109.08, yielding 6.61 percent.
The 2006 benchmark's turnover was 1.6 billion crowns while its June future fell 0.48 point to 108.48 with 25 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.70 point to 87.48.
The crown traded at 3.8065 per mark at 1050 gmt, up a little from around 3.8075 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened one basis point to 70 during the course of the morning.
